analysis.subject: history
analysis.pageCoverage: The page covers the Emancipation Proclamation from preliminary announcement to final issue, its limits as a military measure, and its impact on war aims and Black military service.

overview.headline: Emancipation Proclamation shifted Civil War goals toward freedom and Union strength

keyPoints.point: The North fought to prevent secession and preserve the Union while ending slavery was not an initial goal of the war
keyPoints.quote: ending slavery was not a goal of the war.

keyPoints.point: The Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation issued on September 22, 1862 warned that enslaved people in rebellious areas would be declared free
keyPoints.quote: That changed on September 22, 1862, when President Lincoln issued his Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation

keyPoints.point: As a military measure the Proclamation was limited and left slavery untouched in loyal border states that had seceded from the Union
keyPoints.quote: It applied only to states that had seceded from the Union, leaving slavery untouched in the loyal border states.

keyPoints.point: The Proclamation transformed the war and announced acceptance of Black men into the Union Army and Navy enabling liberated people to become liberators
keyPoints.quote: the Proclamation announced the acceptance of Black men into the Union Army and Navy, enabling the liberated to become liberators.

keyTerms.gloss: withdrawal of Southern states from the Union over sectional conflict and slavery
keyTerms.quote: Initially, the Civil War between North and South was fought by the North to prevent the secession of the Southern states and preserve the Union.

keyTerms.gloss: armed resistance by states still in rebellion against the Union
keyTerms.quote: which stated that enslaved people in those states or parts of states still in rebellion as of January 1, 1863, would be declared free.

keyTerms.gloss: wartime action justified as a military measure to affect the goals of the war
keyTerms.quote: Lincoln’s bold step to change the goals of the war was a military measure

keyTerms.gloss: loyal slaveholding states that remained in the Union and were left untouched by the Proclamation
keyTerms.quote: It applied only to states that had seceded from the Union, leaving slavery untouched in the loyal border states.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Students order causes and effects showing how Union war aims shifted from preserving the Union to including freedom.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Initially, the Civil War between North and South was fought by the North to prevent the secession of the Southern states and preserve the Union.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Students check recall of limits and consequences of the Proclamation through factual question and answer practice.
componentPlan.focusQuote: By the end of the war, almost 200,000 Black soldiers and sailors had fought for the Union and freedom.
